Brisling required only 4.0 decoder passes per utterance compared with Talmar's 37.6, reflecting a large reduction in decoding steps. In terms of accuracy, Brisling's WER of 6.4% was slightly higher than Talmar's 6.1%, but no statistical test was reported, so this difference cannot be claimed as significant. Relative to the Greedy-CTC reference, Brisling achieved a lower WER (6.4% vs 8.9%) at the cost of higher median latency (41 ms vs 22 ms), with both measured on the same hardware.
